statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. NQ futures sit at the top of a narrow overnight band after a completed round trip, and the oil and yield amplifiers that drove the 1-2 September drawdown have both eased, so tail remains inside the low band while stress stays elevated.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON, with one narrow flagged window at 13:30Z-16:00Z on 3 September covering the U.S. cash open, the final services PMI and ISM Services. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Oil and yields ease on an Iran de-escalation hint; NQ futures grind to the top of a narrow overnight band with tail in the low band
body: As of the assessment NQ futures trade at 29,252.00, up 0.23%, inside a 29,132.75-29,253.00 overnight range, quoted at 04:10Z. The overnight path dipped below the 29,186.25 prior settlement to 29,132.75 before fully retracing and grinding to the session high, so the structure is a completed rotation followed by a slow drift rather than persistent directional efficiency. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed the prior session at 29,143.33, up 0.23% inside a 28,971.90-29,165.62 band, snapping a three-session losing streak. The two amplifiers that drove the 1-2 September drawdown have both eased overnight. Brent slipped to about $95.44 and WTI to about $90.91 after President Trump, asked how long renewed strikes on Iran would last, said "I don't think too long"; the 10-year Treasury yield backed off after touching about 4.814% on 2 September, its highest since November 2023, and Japanese government bond yields dipped alongside it. Asian equities advanced, with the Nikkei 225 up 0.2% at 64,455.83, the Hang Seng up 0.7% and the Shanghai Composite up 0.5%, while the yen firmed to about 158.40 per dollar. VIX closed at 15.20, down 6.98%, after fading from a 16.82 session high. Broadcom's 2 September results remain the live single-name driver, with Q3 revenue of $29.6 billion, AI semiconductor revenue of $16.7 billion and Q4 guidance of about $34.8 billion including $21.7 billion of AI semiconductor revenue; the shares round-tripped their after-hours reaction. Latest-session internals were split, with semiconductors leading and software lagging, which argues against aligned one-way structure. Tail therefore stays inside the low band: there is no shallow-pullback, failed-retracement or session-extreme-holding evidence of the kind that denies mean reversion. Stress stays elevated because the energy path, the yield level and the September policy debate are unresolved and August payrolls land on 4 September. The single flagged window is 13:30Z-16:00Z on 3 September, spanning the cash open, the 13:45Z final services PMI and ISM Services at 14:00Z, where an opening auction that converted an event impulse into continuation with shallow pullbacks would be the pattern that changes the assessment.

lookbackSummary: Over the past 24 hours the assessment ran a WATCH stretch in the event/whipsaw regime through the Asian session of 2 September, moved into a trend-down phase during the European morning as oil and yields drove the drawdown, then de-escalated steadily to green EA_ON from about 12:00Z as the rebound produced completed retracements and decaying volatility. The overnight hours settled into a normal, low-volatility regime with tail between 11% and 13%. Five clock-hours have no published assessment and are marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The base case over the next 24 hours is continued two-way price discovery with tail inside the low band through the Asian and European sessions, then one narrow flagged window on 3 September at 13:30Z-16:00Z. That window stacks the U.S. cash open at 13:30Z, the final S&P Global services PMI at 13:45Z and ISM Services at 14:00Z, and it is where an opening auction could convert an event impulse into continuation with shallow pullbacks. Conditional tail enters the watch band across 13:00Z-15:00Z and eases afterwards on the assumption that retracements complete and volatility decays. Stress stays elevated throughout because the energy path, the 10-year yield near its highest since November 2023 and the September policy debate are unresolved, and it firms again late in the U.S. session and through the Asian hours as August payrolls approach on 4 September. The published path deliberately ends before that release rather than assuming its outcome. Confidence starts high on verified futures, cash-close, volatility, rate, oil and calendar evidence and decays with forecast distance.
